The account of her meeting with Mary, in a moment of trial, expresses her direct style in her relationship with her:

“I went to the feet of the Sorrowful Virgin: I must abandon my children; your Son commands it of me through his Vicar... You, Mother, have known the abandonment of Jesus... My Mother, what a knife is this?... I remained absorbed... in the Most Holy Virgin; from her I gained peace and strength. When I came to myself I found myself transformed, a giant” (M. 2, pp. 36-37).

The interior presence of Mary shows her the path to follow, the action to carry out, the conduct to adopt, the patient waiting to be lived in trial:

“...she showed me... these words: ‘Whoever fights under this Standard (the cross) will always be victorious.’ Oh, what I felt...” (M. 12.2, p. 34).

2. THE MOTHER WITH THE CHILD, AND THE ETERNAL FATHER.

In some experiences of infused contemplation Rosa sees the Mother with the Child beside the divine Father. It is a presence which leads us to consider the nature of the bond that associates them in the Economy of Salvation, and which is an existential message for her:

“I saw my Eternal Father with a smiling face; he was pointing out to me a vacant place; and then Mary with my Child Jesus in her arms, in the act of handing him to me...” (M. 1.1, p. 39).

God’s Economy in her regard shows a link between her life and that of Mary with the Child.

In the light of the History of Salvation, the Mother with the Child and the presence of the Eternal Father attest to the reality of Mary in God, who from eternity conceived and created her with the most high dignity of being Mother of the Son, begotten and not made (1).

For Rosa, therefore, in the perspective of the gift received, Mary is the Mother of Jesus, her Son and the eternal Son of the Father; she is the Mother of God, with her most high dignity in heaven and on earth, in her mission and role, with regard to creation and to the plan of the Incarnation and Redemption (2).

3. MARY, MATERNAL SUPPORT IN TRIAL.

Precisely because Mary is Mother of the Incarnate Word, she has become a maternal presence for all people and for Rosa, who experiences this:

“Mary came to comfort me; she appeared to me with the Child in her arms; I was strengthened in a singular way to bear very cruel tribulations” (M. 1.1, p. 101).

This identity of Mary as Mother (3) and her mission, in God’s plan, of bringing to fulfillment, with Jesus, the work of the Father for the salvation of all, is alive in Rosa’s soul.

The presence of Mary as Mother is a source of renewed energy, of comfort, of light and vigor in her mission and offering. Sustained and guided by her maternal presence and intercession, love and dedication to Jesus grow in her. Her illuminations, indications and desires are the foundation of her adherence to God’s plan.

4. WITH THE MOTHER AND THE CHILD IN POVERTY.

Through a vision of Mary with the Child, Saint Joseph and the shepherds of Bethlehem, she learns in an unforgettable way the value of poverty of spirit.

The details present there bring out the poor who are close to Jesus, and let us glimpse her process of purification in order to be welcomed by Him and by Mary:

“...I found myself at the crib, but it seemed to me that Jesus and Mary too... were more pleased with the shepherds... I went to the feet of Saint Joseph and begged him to cover my vileness and obtain for me from the Most Holy Virgin that I might remain at the feet of Jesus... All at once both the Mother and the Son changed... and showed themselves so sweet to me...” (M. 11.2, pp. 11-12).

The symbolism of the seriousness of the face of the Mother and of the Son calls her to conversion, challenges her, makes her attentive to giving room to those present, to not separating the faith and love she has for Jesus and Mary from love for others.

She learns from the Mother and the Son the way of humility, of descent (4), of losing one’s life for others in order to find it again. She learns from the Mother, associated with the life of the Son, to become attentive, gentle, to give joy and room to the humble and the poor, following the indications of the self-lowering of God, who finds delight in the absolute poverty and gratuitousness of Mary (5).

Rosa, after being purified, finds herself at Mary’s feet more humble, at peace, free, and enjoys the joy of the little ones. Thus she enters with her whole self into the mystery of the birth of Jesus, the Poor One of the Father.

The event of Christmas, reported also by the Gospels, asserts itself with all its truth, efficacy and overwhelming relevance in her life: it is the poor who recognize in the Mother with the Child the One and the woman who had been promised by God to save the world, winning the victory over evil (Gen 3:15).

5. MARY WITH THE CHILD AND THE ANCIENT ADVERSARY.

In the Mother and the Child all the promises of the Father are fulfilled with infinite mercy and humility. The motherhood of Mary is the privileged vehicle for bringing about God’s entry into history and his triumph over the evil one (6).

In the womb of the woman who was to crush the head of the serpent the Son of God truly took flesh, not disdaining human frailty (7).

The way of triumph over evil passes through this total dedication to humanity. Mary as Mother is the tangible sign of the infinite mercy of God and the infinite humility of the God-Man, who pitched his tent among us (8).

Rosa receives as a gift the certainty that in weakness there triumphs the strength of the presence and intercession of the Mother of Christ:

“...new tribulations came upon me which tore me apart, so strong were they..., but dear Mother Mary did not delay in coming to comfort me, appearing to me together with the dear Child, my Beloved. Oh, what comfort! But the evil serpent... kept bringing new torments...” (M. 1.1, p. 55).

The work which God accomplished in Mary by associating her with the saving mystery of the Son has permanent value. The efficacy of the Mother’s mission, for every time and for every person who lets himself be docilely guided by her, is for Rosa an experience which gives rise to full adherence to the Economy of God, who sends the Son to bring it to fulfillment: “Behold, there comes into the world a Son, the ‘seed of the woman,’ who will overcome the evil of sin at its roots: ‘he will crush the head of the serpent’... Mary, Mother of the Word, is placed at the center of that enmity, of that struggle which accompanies the history of humanity on earth and the history of salvation itself” (RM 1).

6. THE IMMACULATE MOTHER AND SAINT ANNE.

Mary is a sign that unveils to Rosa the meaning of another Presence through which the mercy of the Lord has passed into the world.

It is Mary, in fact, who introduces her to the knowledge of her own Mother: the Woman who represents the people of God awaiting the coming of the Messiah.

That she might be Mother of the Messiah, God preserved her from original sin in the womb of Anne. She wants Rosa to understand this mystery also in its historical roots, as the fruit of God’s gratuitous love and of the fidelity of a people. Rosa must therefore contemplate it within the universal horizon, both transcendent and historical.

Mary, presenting in a vision her Mother Anne as the spiritual guide of the nascent Work, exhorts Rosa to hold in the highest regard all of God’s interventions in the history of Salvation and the faithful response of the people who welcome the Messiah into their midst (9):

“...I felt so intimate a union with God, when the little chapel was lit up by a great light, and there appeared to me the Most Holy Virgin and Saint Anne... The Immaculate, distinctly, in a clear voice: I desire that the title of the Rules be Daughters of Saint Anne, my Mother (and here she pointed her out to me); I yield this Work with great satisfaction to my Mother” (M. 2, pp. 58-59).

The Immaculate whom she loves, the Chosen One of God, preserved from sin, the Most Holy Virgin, the Mother of Jesus, thus shows her that the Father, in his design of love, wishes to exalt Anne too, her Mother. He wishes to speak a word to the Church and to the world about Anne. He wishes the poor and the suffering to know and venerate the one who collaborated with Him so that the creature chosen to be the Mother of Jesus might be kept whole, humble, faithful to the Covenant and open to the promises of the Messiah, Servant and Savior of the world.

Rosa welcomes the will of the Father, who sends her into the world as a sign and prolongation of the motherhood of Anne, a reflection of his fatherhood. From this fatherhood, in fact, the source and origin of all fatherhood and motherhood on earth, there derives the maternal identity and mission of Mary, the maternal event of Anne. It is an event which brings into the world the one who by pure grace was conceived without sin, as the humblest creature and the one most capable of receiving the ineffable gift of the Almighty (10).

This mystery of the fatherhood of God, made manifest in the motherhood of Anne and above all in that of Mary, is welcomed by Rosa, who celebrates it with her life and works in the Church and in the world.

The motherhood of Anne, in fact, is also a reflection of the divine motherhood of Mary: since she was predestined from eternity as Mother of the Divine Redeemer (LG 61), as such she qualifies the motherhood of Anne and makes it an expression of the one eternal motherhood.

7. MARY, THE MOST HOLY VIRGIN.

The Virginity of Mary is a sign of transparent love, of life lived in God, of the state of life of Jesus, of the new and definitive world, of a form of existence, of the bond between heaven and earth.

This privilege of Mary is frequently brought out by Rosa in her writings:

“...the Most Holy Virgin assured me that she will always be with me...”;

“...the Most Holy Virgin appeared to me”;

“...I was assisted by my Good and by the Most Holy Virgin; never had I had her so near as to feel her love... in my soul”;

“...a joy of love, because comforted... by the Most Holy Virgin” (M. 2, pp. 38; 58; M. 9.8, pp. 50-55).

The Mother of Jesus, therefore, is invoked by Rosa also with the title of Most Holy Virgin. The aspect of the mystery of Mary announced by Isaiah: “Behold: the Virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, whom she shall call Emmanuel” (Is 7:14), brings out and affirms God’s lordship over the world through the person of Mary, his exclusive possession, the land where the Eternal meets the human, surpassing every law inherent in creation.

Thus there rises up in history the Virgin, the exalted daughter of Zion, who becomes the Mother after the long expectation of the promise, when the Son of God takes human nature in her and the times are fulfilled (11).

The mystery announced by Isaiah finds its reflection in the exaltation of the Virgin in the Gospel of Luke: the Virgin of the house of David, the Virgin whose name was Mary (cf. Lk 1:26-27); in the Gospel of Matthew: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary to yourself... what is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit” (Mt 1:20); and in the teaching of the Church: “Thus the Blessed Virgin too advanced in her pilgrimage of faith and faithfully preserved her union with her Son unto the cross, where, not without a divine plan, she stood... with her Only-begotten...” (LG 58).

This mystery of Mary’s virginal life is present in Rosa’s mystical experience and in her existence.

8. WITH MARY MATER GRATIAE ET MISERICORDIAE.

The privilege of Mary, Mother of Grace and of Mercy, expresses her dignity and role in the Economy of Salvation: “By conceiving Christ, bringing him forth... suffering with her Son as he died, ...she cooperated in a wholly singular way in the work of the Savior... to restore supernatural life to souls. For this reason she has been a Mother to us in the order of grace”; – “And this motherhood of Mary in the Economy of grace lasts without interruption... until the eternal crowning of all the elect” (LG 61; 62).

Rosa enjoys the gift of the presence of Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae, which reveals her role in relation to the Church and to all humanity: She cooperated in a special way in the work of the Savior by her obedience, faith, hope and burning charity, so that every person might become a son in the Son (12).

Rosa treasures the presence of the Mother of Grace and of Mercy not only in her heart, but also in her image.

Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae accompanies her in the development of the work and on her personal journey:

“My angel Bernardo appeared to me with his little Madonna...”;

“Oh Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae! Behold, she appeared to me and assured me of the healing...”;

“She gave me strength...”;

“...behold the little Madonna...! The Child held in his hand a chalice which he wanted to hand to me..., and She was holding him. It was a moving sight..., dear Mary prevails” (M. 1.1, p. 83; 5.1, p. 146-147; 5.1, p. 100).

Mary does not abandon Rosa until the very last instant of her life. Her last greeting is for Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae (13). The grace and mercy of God mediated by Mary envelops her throughout her life. What for others is an object of faith is for her an experience: “Not only is the dignity of this motherhood unique and unrepeatable in the history of the human race, but Mary’s participation in God’s plan for man’s salvation through the mystery of the Redemption is also unique... The Father’s eternal love comes close to each of us through this Mother...” (RH 22).

9. MARY, QUEEN OF HEAVEN.

The Father willed to show Rosa also the presence of Mary, Queen of heaven.

Mary, Mother, Immaculate, virgin, Queen of the Universe, associated with the glory of her Son, is contemplated also in this aspect of the fullness of her glory:

“I saw so beautiful a feast in Heaven; the Sovereign Mary is seated at the Right Hand...”;

“...I saw the Sovereign Lady of heaven and earth surrounded by Angels and Seraphim! Oh beloved Mother...” (M. 1.1, p. 153);

“I had the consolation of seeing the commemoration in heaven of the Sovereign Virgin”;

“A fire was devouring me...” (M. 1.1, pp. 38, 153; 12.1, p. 145).

The vision of the fullness of the mystery of Mary associated with the Mystery of the Son is for Rosa a radiance of the Trinitarian Life, present in grace and mercy, in the divine motherhood which, in Christ, with Christ and through Christ, is present in the begetting of all the children of God.

Mary, by introducing her Mother into the life of Rosa Gattorno, shows her a precise will of the Father.

The words she addresses to her in a vision (1), indicating Saint Anne as Mother of the Foundation, she speaks in the name of God himself.

It is truly the Father’s will that Rosa should contemplate certain aspects and prerogatives of his divine Person through the spiritual profile of Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate.

It is God who places Rosa under the maternal protection and spiritual guidance of the Mother of the one who gave the Savior to the world.

1. THE FEATURES OF GOD IN SAINT ANNE.

In the life of Saint Anne God manifests to Rosa his presence and his face.

In the Saints it is He himself who speaks to the Church and to humanity, shows the characteristics of his Kingdom and, through their witness, arouses in the hearts of the faithful a powerful attraction towards himself (2).

Anne enters Rosa’s mystical horizon, the first time, intimately associated with her Daughter Mary and with the presence of Saint Francis of Assisi.

The details described in M. 2, p. 57, already cited, bring out, as was seen in the preceding chapter, the maternal dimension of the Marian mystery reflected in the motherhood of Saint Anne, the line of the Covenant and of the Expectation in the History of Salvation, and also the aspect of poverty of spirit, accentuated by the presence of Saint Francis of Assisi:

“...there appeared to me the Most Holy Virgin and Saint Anne and, lower down, as if he were on his knees towards the Most Holy Virgin, Saint Francis of Assisi...”.

If God radiates himself in his saints, of what aspect of himself, then, does he wish to speak through the presence of Anne?

Anne is first of all the Mother of Mary. As such, her identity is to be placed in the line of the maternal mission, as has already been shown.

Her sharing in the life of God and in his saving economy, as part of the chosen people, reveals in Anne a belonging to him in her life. Her life is a fruit that springs from the condition in which Israel was placed by the God of the Exodus and of the Covenant.

Anne belongs to the faithful Remnant of Israel; she founds her life on God’s fidelity to his promises. She remains faithful to the commitments of the Covenant and awaits the fulfillment of God’s promises. She is certain that he will remember his mercy.

Her waiting rests on the historical experience that Israel had of God. With her people she has experience of his love and of his forgiveness.

God is the cause, the soul and the end of her existence. She walks with her God in the awareness of his divine transcendence, and she knows that He can break in with something new and lead her along unknown ways.

Anne is the woman of Hope which rests on the experience of the Covenant: she walks with God the Creator, Savior, Redeemer and Spouse who forgives and shows mercy, who establishes the Kingdom founded on justice, on love and on universal brotherhood, and above all on the presence of God.

In Saint Anne there is the dawn of the day on which: “...the peoples shall see your justice, and all kings your glory; you shall be called by a new name which the mouth of the Lord will give... No more shall you be called Forsaken, nor shall your land any more be called Desolate, but you shall be called my delight and your land Espoused, for the Lord will delight in you and your land shall have a spouse...” (Is 62:2.4).

Anne is the daughter of Abraham, of David; she is a member of a people of the poor who with trust await and receive Salvation from him; she is the one who gives birth to the Handmaid of the Lord and who awaits the Messiah-Servant, the Savior, the Redeemer, the Priest of the New and eternal Covenant.

God, therefore, manifests in the life of Anne his presence and his face as merciful Father, Father of the humble and the poor. Father of the Poor Handmaid who “stands out among the humble,” Father of the Son-Servant, Crucified and Savior of the world (3).

2. SAINT ANNE AND THE VENERABLE BERNARDO M. CLAUSI.

After the first vision of Saint Anne with Mary Most Holy and Saint Francis of Assisi, Rosa’s relationship with her becomes ever deeper and more intense. Above all it is the Father who grants the Holy Mother of Mary to be a special Presence in Rosa’s life and mission.

In one of the first visions of Saint Anne, she appears to her together with the Venerable Bernardo Maria Clausi, of the Minims of Saint Francis of Paola (4). He is known to Rosa through the mediation of Father Giovanni Battista Tornatore (5). She knows that he greatly loved Saint Anne during his earthly life and that he had even prophesied the rise of a Work dedicated to her.

Well then, of this figure Rosa describes the experience of his presence beside the Holy Mother of Mary:

“While I was in the little Chapel of Saint Joseph... Saint Anne appeared to me, and on the left side of the Saint there was Father Bernardo. Both very beautiful, with a most vivid light. Saint Anne held a book in her hand and was in the act of handing it to me. Father Bernardo said to me: ‘Go to Father Tornatore and tell him to give you the book he has for this foundation,’ and he disappeared. I was left full of consolation and trust” (M. 1.1, p. 91).

After the first meeting, Bernardo will be one of God’s messengers for Rosa. He will enlighten her on certain aspects of her mission in the Church, and by his presence he will bear witness to her of her identification with certain aspects of the Mystery of Christ, of the Trinity, and with the Motherhood of Mary.

He is the one who in God’s name shows Rosa which person is to collaborate with her in drawing up the Constitutions.

As Moses is the charismatic and the Prophet of his people, and God always speaks with him, even though he gives him a collaborator in Aaron to convey God’s messages to Pharaoh and to the people, so Rosa is the charismatic with whom God speaks directly; yet she too receives the collaboration of Father Tornatore so that the charism may be formulated with theological competence.

God, who in his saving economy has created and creates people with different functions so that they may collaborate with him, in Christ and in the Holy Spirit, in building up the Kingdom (6), accompanies the development of the Work entrusted to Rosa Gattorno with the help of these persons specially prepared by him.

3. SAINT ANNE, MOTHER AND SPIRITUAL GUIDE.

Rosa lives devotion to Saint Anne as a filial relationship and one of discipleship. Her way of relating to her finds a parallel in the teaching of the Church, which forms the faithful in the true cult of the Saints. The cult of the Saints does not consist in the multiplying of external acts, but rather in the intensity of an active love, by which, for the greater good of each one and of the Church, we seek communion with them, a share in their life and the help of their intercession (7).

From the description Rosa has left of the presence of Saint Anne in her life there shine through the values which she develops by living in communion with her:

“The calumnies were terrible; (with reference to these) Mother Saint Anne consoled me, saying to me: ‘My daughter, who has been more calumniated than I?’. While I was to bear the most precious fruit of the Eternal Father; and this gave me strength and patience to bear everything” (M. 1.1, p. 126).

This confidence is enough for Rosa to learn to bear everything, loving and forgiving after the example of the Holy Mother. Jesus himself, in infused contemplation, makes known to her certain aspects of the life of Saint Anne:

“...I stayed there listening to what my Beloved was teaching me, and it was concerning Saint Anne and what I was to say. So sublime was his speech that, on coming back to myself, there were so many things I did not understand, and I could not grasp their meaning. Ah! My most Beloved all did not delay in teaching me... in opening my intellect to knowledge and to the capacity to discern. Then I went over all that I had heard, word by word, and saw very well what he wanted me to do...” (M. 4.1, p. 82 f.).

What she lives confirms that the mission of the Saints in the Church and in the world is a sacrament of that of Christ and of his Spirit.

It is therefore the Beloved himself, with the Holy Spirit, who are at work in her life through the presence of Anne.

The Spirit, in Anne, shows her the will of the Father and gives her forewarning of the events that weave the history of the Church, her own history and that of the Work entrusted to her.

Through this divine benevolence, Saint Anne is present in the Work, rejoices in all the good that is done in it, and prepares Rosa to meet adversities with fortitude of soul and to become ever keener in distinguishing good – that which makes the communities advance in holiness – from the evil which offends the Lord and spiritually destroys persons.

This is how she depicts the presence of Saint Anne on her path as foundress:

“...what consolation I felt when the Holy Mother Anne began to laugh and, with a gesture of contentment, consoled me. Ah! my Mother, are you content?...” (M. 4.2, p. 38).

“...my Star, Saint Anne, every morning marks the day for me, because if I am to undergo tribulations she shows herself to me pale and sad; if there is a death, or things which the sisters do that are not right and are against the Holy Rule, she is covered with a black veil...” (M. 4.5, p. 143 f.).

The Holy Mother of Mary is therefore for her a teacher and a maternal guide, a sign of the care which God has for Rosa and for her Work.

She is a presence that points to the Presence of God in her and infinitely above her, to the presence of the Father, of the Son and of the Spirit. She is a sign of their love for the Work which they themselves have raised up in the Church.

4. SAINT ANNE AND THE MISSION TO THE SICK.

As was said before, in the presence of Anne, as in the life of every saint, the divine action of the Father, his will and his holiness, are manifested.

In the signs and interior words by which Saint Anne mystically transmits her message to Rosa, one finds a harmony with the signs and words which she receives directly from the Father, from Christ, from the Spirit and from Mary.

As for her mission to the sick, we have seen how, connected with the blessing of the oil for the sick (8), there is for Rosa the Father’s sending of her to care for the sick.

This same sending He confirms through the person of Saint Anne, who, on a March 1 of which the year cannot be determined, places in Rosa’s hands a supernatural energy: that power of the Spirit which goes out from Christ in his acts of healing and restoration; “...power went out from him and healed them all” (Lk 6:19). (9).

She notes on the page of a notebook the event that concerns her:

“March 1, from the Holy Mother Anne I received in my hands a light, in the center of my hands. And she said: ‘From now on all the sick whom you bless will be healed; always in God’s name you shall bless them and they will be healed’” (10).

It is evident that the Father entrusts to Rosa with special love the care of the sick, and thus makes her a sharer in the very mission of the Son, who “healed them all.”

Of Jesus, the Gospel of Mark underlines: “He laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them”; “He laid his hands on him and asked him: ‘Do you see anything?’” (Mk 6:5; 8:23). To the apostles too Jesus entrusts as a priority the mission of preaching, that people may be converted, of freeing from demons and of healing the sick (cf. Mk 6:12-13).

5. SAINT ANNE, PROTECTRESS OF ROSA AND OF THE WORK.

The Work which arose in the Church by the will of the Father, who, in Jesus Crucified, addresses the call to Rosa: “From you I want this Work,” is placed by his benevolence under the protection of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate.

All the means arranged by God so that the life generated may grow and develop to its full completion are provided for the Work entrusted to Rosa also through the person and intercession of Saint Anne.

She has the clear awareness of being accompanied with tenderness and firmness by the Father, “...like a little girl he led me by the hand in all that I did” (M. 4.2, p. 16 f.), and that much of this support comes to her through Saint Anne.

Reading her Memoirs attentively, one grasps the deep bond that unites Saint Anne to the Work of God:

“This morning, while I was making my meditation, something supernatural came over me that I cannot express. While I was in this union, drowsiness, which I cannot describe well, I saw clearly the Holy Mother Anne praying to the Savior with insistence. At last He answered her: ‘All that you ask of me you shall have.’ How consoled I was by it! I felt a strong sweetness and assurance of having obtained everything through my Holy Mother Anne” (M. 11.3, p. 81).

Affectionately bound to her, in a surge of apostolic zeal Rosa continues the description, grateful for all the graces she bestows on her:

“I would like to be able to make her loved by the whole world. What power she has before the throne of God! Jesus can refuse her nothing. An infinity of times could I describe the great graces which Jesus granted to his Work through the intercession of the Holy Mother!” (M. 11.3, p. 82).

In Rosa’s writings concerning her contemplations of the Holy Mother Anne, one observes that she sees her carrying out a mediation on behalf of the Work. She prays to the Savior to obtain Providence for the Communities and the works, acts for the approval of the Constitutions and protects the Work from dangers. She speaks with her, warning her about failures in observance, or to show her delight at the good done by her daughters and to assure her that the reward for her sharing in the mystery of Christ Crucified and in all the tribulations of the Work and of the Church will be great.

FATHER BERNARDO MARIA CLAUSI,

A PRESENCE IN THE LIFE.

OF ROSA GATTORNO.

The will of God, as has been shown several times, is manifested to men through the life and mission of Christ and of the Holy Spirit. But in his Economy the Father makes the Angels and men sharers in his creative and redemptive work, above all those who by their witness have been or are faithful transmitters of his will.

The Venerable Bernardo Maria Clausi is one of these faithful witnesses of the will of God. He is given by the Father to Rosa as a mystical Presence, to point out to her certain aspects of his divine will and to uphold her in moments of trial.

1. THE VENERABLE BERNARDO MARIA CLAUSI AND SAINT ANNE.

The mystical relationship of the Venerable Bernardo (1) Maria Clausi with Rosa Gattorno is subordinate to the mission he must carry out on behalf of the “Work of Saint Anne,” which in the Church has the aim of prolonging the style of spiritual life of the Family of Saints Anne and Joachim, who lived with Mary intent on the contemplation of God and of his saving works and, loving him, awaited the Messiah. Of the vision in which Father Bernardo Maria Clausi appears to her for the first time, Rosa describes the details most essential and significant in God’s plan and important for the nascent Work:

“At the thought that Pius IX wanted the internal regulations soon, I prayed much but never heard anything. One evening, while I was alone in the Chapel, behold, there appeared to me Saint Anne and Father Bernardo, whom I recognized because Signor Tornatore (2) had given me his portrait. What! saying this I was left confused. Beautiful was the Holy Mother, in the act of caressing me. She came very close to me and communicated to me so strong a love for her... Father Bernardo said these words: ‘The regulations you desire, tell Signor Tornatore to draw them up,’ and they both disappeared” (M. 1.2, pp. 61-62).

The vision confirms Rosa in what Father Tornatore had confided to her about a dream of his – in his view of divine origin (3) – from which he deduced that she was the person chosen by God to found the Work of Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate. For this reason he often spoke to her of the Ideal, cherished by Father Bernardo, of seeing arise in the Church a Work wholly dedicated to the Mother of Mary Immaculate.

2. FATHER BERNARDO AND THE CONSTITUTIONS.

Father Bernardo, once he has entered Rosa’s mystical horizon, becomes the instrument which the Holy Spirit uses to continue his work in the Church also through the new foundation. God had long since arranged everything; now, however, spiritual events and historical times converge in giving shape to the Work.

The initiative is God’s. It is he who, through an interweaving of relationships and events, makes his lordship over the Work stand out. He is always Rosa’s guide, teacher and strength, but in his economy he chooses men and saints, faithful devotees of Saint Anne, in support of the Work, thus standing beside Rosa herself in her mission as foundress.

Bernardo is one of these Presences whom God chooses to be mystically beside Rosa and to recall to her certain aspects of God’s design.

His mission at first concerns the help which Rosa must ask of Father Giovanni Battista Tornatore:

“Oh my mother, I kept exclaiming! I did not have the courage to tell Signor Tornatore what Father Bernardo had told me. I remained so for several months, and a second time he came alone and urged me to go to Signor Tornatore. That I should do it at once...” (M. 2, p. 63).

Seeing her uncertain about presenting the request to him (Rosa always shows herself reluctant to communicate her mystical experiences to others), Father Bernardo presents himself to her frequently, as if to hasten her decision:

“One morning after Holy Communion he came close to me: ‘I say that you must obey.’ I answered him nothing, because I had my God with me and had much to say to him. After some more time, perhaps eight days, so it seems to me, there he was once again. I was finishing my thanksgiving when I heard a voice grumbling brusquely. I looked: it was Father Bernardo. In a resolute tone, in a threatening manner, he said to me: ‘Go at once and tell him that it is I who send you’” (M. 2, p. 64).

Rosa continues the description of the events, adding:

“I went to this Signor Tornatore and told him half of what Father Bernardo had told me. He began to laugh, answering: ‘I will do it.’ So he did. As soon as they were printed I took them to Rome, and for them I received mockery from all the members of the Sacred Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, because they were in the form of a dialogue...” (M. 2, p. 65). (4).

God’s signs are unmistakable; but as happens in the history of Salvation, where the Patriarchs and Prophets, though certain that God has spoken to them, nevertheless find themselves struggling against adverse forces or the conflicts due to different mentalities or experiences, so it happens to Rosa.

The Lord of History permits darkness, but he by no means lets light and strength be lacking to the person whom He himself has drawn into a pact whose constitutive elements remain in spite of every apparent failure. It is the History of the Only-begotten Son, of his mission in the world, which is prolonged in his faithful servants, revealing the same constants of self-emptying and of death, the indispensable condition for definitively conquering death itself.

3. FATHER BERNARDO MARIA CLAUSI AND MARY.

The visions of Father Bernardo are for Rosa a moral support and the bearers of new messages.

Now she sees him “seated upon a light in the manner of a cloud,” at other times with the small picture of the little Madonna, Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae, as if to signify to her his love for Mary (5) and the role which these prerogatives of hers, “grace and mercy,” have in her life:

“Last night, when I was suffering on the cross, I lamented and called on my Eternal Father to come to my aid... I raised my head a little... if it had been possible for me, but not being able to, I stopped at once; there appeared to me my angel, Father Bernardo, with his little Madonna in his hand” (M. 1.1, p. 83).

The sign with which Bernardo presents himself is also an expression of the intensity with which he himself loved Mary with the Child. This love for Mary, Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae, is a feature of his life very close to the loving experience which Rosa has of the same Mother, contemplated in the privileges of “Grace and Mercy,” as well as in other aspects, as her writings show.

The mystical dialogue established between the two concerning Mary is interesting: Rosa, calling on Father Bernardo to give her some flowers, describes the little Madonna as “his and all mine”:

“...I heard something, and it was Father Bernardo. I began to laugh... I was asking him to give me a flower from those I saw at the feet of his little Madonna, who is all mine; they were most beautiful roses and lilies. Why do you not give me one? How miserly you are... and all in jest, because he too was laughing. Oh! your laughter, I fear it may bring me who knows what; but he said nothing to me. It only seemed that he had the mission of keeping me company. The following night he stayed with me with the little Madonna. Oh! what sweetness at once; but then he showed me what was prepared in the way of tribulations and sufferings: at such a sight I trembled all over..., but Mary with her dear and sweet voice consoled me and ... me and so many consoling things” (M. 1.1, p. 132).

As Mary had been, after the Most Holy Trinity, the love and support of Bernardo in the heroic trials of spirit borne during his earthly life, so Rosa often experiences the maternal mediation of Mary in her spiritual growth and in her trials, and also a spiritual affinity with Bernardo, whom God himself has placed at her side like an Angel.

4. FATHER BERNARDO AND THE BLESSED SACRAMENT.

At other moments of infused contemplation, Rosa sees Bernardo with Jesus in the Eucharist.

He appears to her with the Monstrance in moments of great suffering, as if to attest to the intrinsic value of the Eucharist and its importance in their lives: the Victim of the New and Eternal Covenant associates them both in the vocation of “victim” for the Church.

The Eucharist, in fact, is the utmost self-giving of Jesus, who remains in the world silently prolonging his offering until all creation is recapitulated in him.

Bernardo, in his earthly life, was intimately associated with Christ the Victim. Many witnesses attest to this identification of his with the Eucharist: “He was admirable with Jesus in the August Sacrament... When he made us reflect on the immense love which Jesus Christ bore us in instituting the Sacrament, he said things so beautiful, so sublime, so full of unction and sweetness that he enchanted us, and at that moment we believed we loved that Sacrament as he loved it. He seemed another man, he caught fire, he spoke with such a profusion of words that the saying was truly verified that the mouth speaks from the fullness of the heart.” (6).

To this testimony others are added which bring out his Eucharistic sense: “Jesus in the Eucharist, in the offering of the renewed Sacrifice, concentrated and polarized him to the utmost. His Mass was that of the mystic: ecstasy, Eucharistic dialogue, manifestations of his face lit up by a flush that was not a natural effect.” (7).

Other texts of the Process Super Virtutibus add: “One sees him grow in aspirations, ejaculatory prayers... and outpourings of love with God. At times also prostrate on the step of the Altar of the Blessed Sacrament, remaining long in fervent adoration.”

This dimension of Bernardo’s identity remains with him as a seal that distinguishes him from others on the universal horizon of the Church. And, as far as Rosa is granted to contemplate, he shows himself such from Heaven as well. This is how she describes him in her Memoirs:

“On Saturday, when my pains had ceased, not entirely, a little, I remained absorbed and saw Father Bernardo giving me the blessing with the Blessed Sacrament. He seemed to be in the midst of an immense light...” (M. 1.1, p. 121).

The specific presence of Bernardo with the Monstrance confirms Rosa in the importance of the Blessed Sacrament in her life. Jesus, Victim of Love, blesses her by the hand of Bernardo, who in his turn is associated with the divine Victim (8) as she is: both passed through the great trial of the spirit and were tormented by the harassments of the evil one (9).

5. FATHER BERNARDO AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE WORK OF GOD.

The presence of Bernardo in Rosa’s life, as support and guide, seems to alternate with the presence of the Cloud:

“...besides, I always consulted him, as I now consult my Cloud” (M. 1.1, p. 85).

From the prophecies he makes to her about the Work, his mission as a collaborator in the Work of God is evident. Rosa, in fact, notes in her Memoirs another important intervention of his concerning the Work of God:

“Today my Angel, Father Bernardo, appeared to me and showed me another foundation in this City of Piacenza, and these will be cloistered nuns. He explained to me a prophecy of his, which he made when he was in Piacenza with the Caracciolo family” (M. 1.1, p. 90).

Still in line with Bernardo’s prophetic gift, she writes on another occasion:

“I dozed off. I was overtaken by a dream in which a Religious began to tell me various prophecies which Father Bernardo made concerning the Work of Saint Anne... and he went on with his discourse, saying to me: ‘Father Bernardo told me to tell you that this Work will spread throughout the whole world... you will have great consolations to experience...’” (M. 4.3, p. 8 f.).

To these signs are added others concerning his intercession to obtain Providence for the Work. This is how she describes the event of the death of one of the Counts Caracciolo, a benefactor of the Work:

“Today, the 16th, this morning while I was making my thanksgiving after Holy Communion, there appeared to me Father Bernardo Maria Clausi, Venerable, as if he were announcing to me something that had already happened; what is it? I recommend that you take to heart certain persons; and it was as if I felt that he will do it. After a few hours the news came to me of the death of one of the Counts Caracciolo, those who gave much to the Work of Saint Anne” (M. 9.8, p. 37).

In fact, Rosa goes on noting the fulfillment of the messages she receives from Father Bernardo. They are gradually realized, thus confirming her in her trust in him. One important prophecy concerns the very life and holiness of Father Bernardo, whose glory the Lord lets her see:

“He showed me so many things, such as the graces he had prepared for me, and the time when I shall be able to act freely..., the glory which Father Bernardo enjoys in heaven, and that he will be beatified and all doubts will be smoothed away; and so clearly did he show me so many things” (M. 1.1, p. 128).

Finally, the divine message of which Father Bernardo is the expression by his life – in the features of the saints the particular aspects of the mystery of Christ are revealed – builds Rosa up on her path towards holiness and lets her experience a spiritual harmony with him.

Bernardo Maria Clausi, from the profile sketched in the Novissima Positio Bernardi Mariae Clausi, emerges as an outstanding figure who, by his spiritual features and apostolic ardor, expresses a particular aspect of spiritual theology. He cherishes a special communion with the Most Holy Trinity, with Jesus considered in the mystery of the Incarnation, of the Passion and in the Eucharist, with Mary Most Holy, above all in her maternal dimension.

He cultivates an important relationship with Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, whom he calls the Grandmother, and in her honor he has a Hail Mary recited after the prayer of the Angelus, to thank her for having given us a beautiful Mother in her Daughter; and also a special devotion to Saint Joseph, Saint Francis of Paola and Saint Michael the Archangel.

He is the man who lives with heroic fidelity the virtues and the religious commitments and receives in his turn great charismatic gifts: prophecy, a fire of love that consumes him, the reading of hearts, the power to free the possessed, fortitude in bearing and overcoming diabolical harassments upon his own person. He shares in the sorrows of the Church – he was intimately persuaded that he was the cause of all the evils that happened in the world and in the Church... – he feels himself unworthy of God and his adversary (antichrist), he undergoes the great trial: to be convinced that by divine justice he is destined to suffer an exemplary damnation...

He mortifies himself with the discipline to the point of blood; he is a poor man, most humble, meek, heroic in faith, hope and charity, prudent, just and simple; in the great trial he repeats: “I am a sinner, but holy purity I have never stained.”

CHAPTER SEVENTEEN.

THE ANGELS IN THE MYSTICISM OF ROSA GATTORNO.

In his Economy, God has entrusted to the Angels the mission of collaborating with him in the plan of Salvation. The role of the Angels is amply manifest throughout the history of Salvation.

In the New Testament the Angels appear above all at the service of the mission of Christ, of his conception, his birth, resurrection and ascension; they are the object of the preaching of Jesus himself (1).

In Rosa’s life one perceives a progression of this presence of “heavenly beings” who announce to her the visit of God.

1. THE ANGELS, MESSENGERS OF HER DESTINY IN GOD.

Associated with other mystical events, particular experiences with the Angels of God emerge in Rosa’s life. In the first visions she contemplates them, but giving greater attention to the functions they carry out with regard to her mission. They are for her the bearers of a message (2) which she describes thus:

“He showed me two books which were held by two Angels... I saw them with the blood of my Redeemer...” (M. 1.1, p. 5).

This vision is followed by another, with a symbol that is expressive and important for her vocation in Christ:

“After Holy Communion, one day, I saw two Angels approach with a crown of thorns in their hands, which resembled that of my Beloved” (M. 1.1, p. 7).

The symbolism of the Angels with the crown returns several times in her mystical experience, in her mature years as well. One day, as the Eternal Father’s answer to her plea to be granted the gift of carrying the cross, she receives the sign:

“I saw one (a cross) so large that it was carried by two Angels, and they were holding it out to me; it had the three nails fixed in it; what gladness I felt!” (M. 1.1, p. 15).

The presence of the Angels is therefore for her the experience of a message of God’s design, a sign that points to another Presence and to involvement in the saving mission of Jesus (3).

2. ANGELS WITH THE CHALICE.

Continuing to observe these presences along the line of the symbols they bear and which express a message from God, there follows a vision of the great agony of Jesus in the garden, with the presence of the Angel bearing the Chalice in his hand. Several times one observes, in the extraordinary expressions God uses to communicate with Rosa, the centrality of the Chalice.

Precisely the Chalice, the symbol par excellence, with which Jesus celebrates the New and Eternal Covenant: “He took the Chalice.”

The Father, therefore, prepares her to drink the Chalice with Jesus:

“...I had before me the Angel who held the Chalice in his hand. Oh! how willingly I would have drunk it myself!” (M. 1.2, p. 5).

In another vision the Angel is also the bearer of bread. Rosa experiences what the Bible proclaims: “Man ate the bread of Angels” (Ps 78:25); “You fed your people with the food of Angels; from heaven you offered them bread ready to hand, without toil, able to give every delight and to satisfy every taste” (Wis 16:20).

And especially the words of Jesus are, in the experience she describes, a reality for her: “My Father gives you the bread from heaven, the true bread... I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never thirst” (Jn 6:32-35).

This is how Rosa describes God’s intervention, mediated by an Angel who feeds and sustains her:

“On January 30 there appeared to me a very tall Angel; he had a blue mantle and a sky-blue sash and a most beautiful golden baldric. He gave me three small pieces of bread to eat (Oh! how exquisite it was). I must say: I was so exhausted and seemed to be dying, alone in my room... second, it seemed to me that it would take little for me to expire. Then he appeared to me, comforting me because I was suffering. When I had finished eating this bread he showed me a full Chalice and said to me: ‘This you will have to swallow entirely’... and again I fell into agony; I could say nothing, I only felt in me an ardor to swallow it all, while it seemed to me that he was bringing it near for me to drink. I fainted and remained leaning on his shoulder. I had not entirely lost my senses, because I felt the Chalice brought to my lips, as if I had swallowed it all... ‘You must swallow it all,’ so he said to me” (M. 1.2, p. 34 f.). (4).

The experience of light alternates with that of darkness. In the mystic the existential conflict of the universe is repeated, the clash of light with darkness. The experience of light, in fact, of the messenger of God, providence, beauty reflected in the features of the Angel, the physician who feeds her with the “bread of heaven” and with the chalice of participation in the covenant of the Supreme and Eternal Priest, is the prelude to the hour of darkness (5).

The enemy enters the field, assails her and engages her in the struggle, the very one which he has always waged against God, against his Christ and against the children of men.

This is how she continues to describe the unfolding of the mystical event:

“When I came to myself he vanished, and I remained alone, like one who is still between sweetness and suffering, but greatly strengthened; I no longer felt myself fainting... I fell asleep, but always as if I had that Angel near... Oh! the following night, what a terrible night! what a battle, what cruel torments the enemy made me feel... every kind of suggestion, of torment he inflicted on me...” (M. 1.2, pp. 34-35).

But on p. 17, M. 4.1, speaking of the Angel who cares for her and sustains her, she says: “The Angel whom my Jesus gave me guards me very well... he even seems to give me more strength to be able to do everything without lying down... You are strong and powerful, my dear Raphael.”

3. THE ARCHANGEL MICHAEL, GUARDIAN OF THE WORK.

The identity of the mission entrusted to her by God can be grasped in every mystical event she describes. The lordship of God and his protection over Israel, exercised also through the powerful mediation of the Angels, now extends over the Church and, with various particular features, over each of her members.

Upon Rosa it rests with symbols and presences which belonged to the children of Israel. God accompanies her on her pilgrimage with his Angel Michael. He, described in the Bible as the Angel of Yahweh, opposes Satan; he is the Angel who protects the people of God and the One who fights with his Angels against the dragon (6).

The experience in which the Archangel Michael enters her life offers elements that link it with the biblical experiences:

“Before leaving for Foligno-Rome, I was asking my Eternal all to assist me and grant me the good fortune of making a good journey. While I was saying to him: stretch out your right hand and defend me from dangers, something came forward that was troubled, or to say it better, confused, but I understood little: an Angel who was giving me help... Only when I was on the steamer did this thing come to me again more clearly. My God, who is this Angel? let me see him. But nothing. At last I realized that I had two, but I did not see well what he was like. Having reached a city where I spent the night..., at last, in the morning I went to receive Communion, and after a little while: ‘My Good, who is that Angel I see around me...?’ A most clear Voice answered me: ‘He is mine...’” (M. 4.1, p. 13 f.).

He is the Angel from whom Rosa hears it said: “From now on, by order of my God, I shall be your guide, your companion on your long journeys” (7); he is the one who defeats the forces of evil, he is the adorer of God: “who is like God?”, the “liberator of those who fear the Lord.”

Well then, Rosa experiences how Saint Michael the Archangel is the defender of God, the protector of the Work and her protector too. He sustains her in her self-surrender, which, precisely because it is acceptable to God, carries within it the clash with the forces of darkness.

The description Rosa gives of the Presence of Michael and of his particular mission against the enemy of God is lucid and detailed, in spite of the trembling, the disgust and the terror that invade her:

“I was commending myself to my Guardian Angel, and still more to the one my Jesus gave me, Michael the Archangel: ‘Ah, take up your sword...,’ and saying this I kept my eyes turned towards heaven (turned, that is, in the room where I was). I saw a group of demons (8) all naked... they fell headlong one upon another. The Angel Michael, who was killing them with his sword (but he only made the gesture of this killing, he did not touch them...)” (M. 4.1, p. 54 f.).

Rosa’s experience attests that the biblical message about the identity of Michael is a reality. Jesus himself, who asked her to write down her experiences, gives a further confirmation of what the Holy Spirit has handed on and hands on, through the Bible, to the humanity of all ages.

The Church takes up this revelation in her Magisterium in order to enlighten the faithful about the struggle which the evil one, the adversary of Christ, wages against men, but also that God always remains the Lord, the master of every dark force, the defender of those who entrust themselves to him.

4. THE ANGELS MICHAEL AND GABRIEL AT PRAYER.

On Rosa’s mystical horizon the messages which God offers through his Angels continue. In each of her experiences it is evident that all the signs serve God’s plan and are at the service of her life and of the Work.

The presence of the Angels, therefore, is ordered to a mission willed by God. The gift he grants her in the month of March 1875 is truly surprising:

“One day I went to make my communion..., in this month of March 1875. It did not seem to me that I had prepared myself well, because I was very ill; I could say little to my Good, I only offered him the suffering I had, but I harbored a certain fear of not being able to make my thanksgiving; in short, I was greatly troubled; but as soon as I had received him I saw at my side the Angel Michael, who was making the thanksgiving together with me and, with hands joined, was adoring God. At that sight I felt a certain gladness...” (M. 4.3, p. 29).

The Lord lets her live another experience of the same kind with the Angel Gabriel; he thus shows the bond that exists, in God’s Economy, between the Angels and humanity.

Rosa writes with sincerity what her Good grants her:

“This evening, tired in mind from having worked so much..., I found it hard to gather my thoughts and find the point of the meditation. My mind wandered, leaping now here, now there...; I was sorry because I did not find that union, and I remained fearful, but calm. A most beautiful Angel appeared to me who, near me, was praying. Why, I asked him, was he doing this? He answered me nothing, but an inner voice said to me: ‘He is praying for you; he does what you cannot do; he makes up for it. Your weariness is very pleasing to the Lord; therefore this Angel Gabriel takes your place.’ I remained so content within, and as if I had tasted what I could have felt in union” (M. 9.7, p. 5 ff.). (9).

5. THE JOY OF THE ANGELS IN CELEBRATION.

Besides being God’s messengers for her mission, the Angels offer Rosa flashes of deep joy, anticipating moments of the blessedness without end. This is how she describes a moment of communion with her Good, who is granting her to see a glimpse of eternity:

“On the day of the Immaculate I added to my vows that of poverty (year 1862)..., the rapture increased..., I felt that something was to happen in me... I saw the feast that was being prepared in heaven. Oh! immense joy: the Saints who had greater splendor, the Angels with garlands were going about crowning them; the melody of the sounds; the souls who dwell in Paradise vied with one another to celebrate their advocates. Oh! Paradise, how beautiful you are: your joys and your feasts make me die!... the sight of my Good..., so beautiful, those rays, that light, the beauty...!” (M. 1.1, p. 41). (10).

Also in one of the visions of Father Bernardo, on the day when he prophesies to her the foundation of the contemplative community in Piacenza and explains to her the prophecy he made when he was visiting the Caracciolo Family, Rosa notes:

“Today I heard the music of the Angels” (M. 1.1, p. 90).

On another most beautiful occasion, while she is contemplating the Incarnation of the Word, she takes part in the feast of the Angels, which she describes thus:

“For two days I always had a company of Angels who stayed near me; they rejoiced around me while I contemplated the mystery of the Incarnation in the womb of Mary Most Holy” (M. 9.8, p. 5 f.).

Thus there resounds for her the inspired Word: “God... when he brings the firstborn into the world, says: – Let all the Angels of God adore him..., while of the Angels he says: – He makes his Angels winds, and his ministers a flame of fire” (Heb 1:5-7).

Through the mystical experience of Rosa Gattorno it has been possible to glimpse the supernatural horizon within which she lived in depth her relationship with the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit, Mary, Mother of Jesus and daughter of St. Anne, the Saints, the Angels, and the Church.

Her very person appears as a human space in which the Lord was pleased to manifest aspects of his divine reality and of his saving plan for the Church and for the whole human family.

Her “Good,” Father, Son, beloved Spouse of hearts, divine Fire, governing Spirit, strength and Sweetness beyond compare, drew her into his mission as Victim of Love.

And she, letting herself be drawn in, like the Prophet, proclaimed with her life: “You have seduced me, Lord, and I let myself be seduced” (Jer 20:7).

From her progressive, intense, docile, unconditional welcome of the life of God and of its demands there sprang her active, dynamic, creative response, which made her one “of the most beautiful and generous souls of the second half of the last century.” (1).

Seeking the good pleasure of her “Supreme Good” in action as much as in contemplation, Rosa genuinely commented with her life on the words of Jesus to Martha, in defense of Mary’s attitude: “...she has chosen the better part” (Lk 10:42).
